record.context_brief: Treating the deformation parameter as a parameter
record.original_question: For generalized exponential families such as q-exponential or lambda-exponential families, is there a systematic way to treat the deformation parameter itself as an additional parameter rather than fixing it in advance?

evidence.quote: Is there a systematic way to study the deformation parameter as another parameter?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be a deformation function depending on a real parameter $\kappa$ (for example $\Phi_q(x)=x^q$ giving rise to the $q$-exponential $\exp_q(x)=(1+(1-q)x)_+^{1/(1-q)}$, or the $\lambda$-exponential $\exp_\lambda$ used in $\lambda$-deformed exponential families). For a fixed value of $\kappa$, the associated deformed exponential family on a sample space $\mathcal{X}$ is
$$p_\kappa(x;\theta)=\exp_\kappa\!\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n\theta^i F_i(x)-\psi_\kappa(\theta)\Big),\qquad \theta\in\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^n,$$
together with its induced information geometry (Fisher–Rao metric, dual affine connections, divergence, etc.).

Standard treatments fix the deformation parameter $\kappa$ in advance and study the resulting $n$-parameter statistical manifold. 

Question: Provide a systematic framework in which the deformation parameter $\kappa$ itself is treated as an additional coordinate of the statistical manifold, so that one studies the enlarged $(n+1)$-parameter family $\{p_\kappa(x;\theta):(\theta,\kappa)\in\Theta\times K\}$. In particular, define the corresponding Fisher information matrix, dual connections, potential function, and divergence on the enlarged manifold, and describe the geometric structures (such as dual flatness, curvature, or conformal structure) that arise when $\kappa$ varies, together with the limiting behavior as $\kappa$ approaches the classical exponential case.
artifact.category_tag: information geometry of deformed exponential families
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on $q$-exponential, $\lambda$-exponential, and $\phi$-deformed exponential families consistently treats the deformation parameter as fixed and develops information geometry on the resulting $n$-parameter manifold. No systematic framework treating the deformation parameter as an additional coordinate of the statistical manifold appears to be established; the question is posed as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of q-Exponential Family of Probability Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: An information-geometrical foundation is established for deformed exponential families... with q treated as a fixed deformation parameter.
status_evidence.claim: Standard treatments fix q and study the resulting parameter manifold.

status_evidence.title: λ-Deformed probability families with subtractive and divisive normalizations
status_evidence.snippet: The induced information geometry of λ-deformed exponential families has a pair of constant-curvature dual connections... where the λ parameter encodes the curvature value.
status_evidence.claim: λ is treated as a fixed deformation parameter encoding curvature, not as an additional manifold coordinate.

status_evidence.title: Information Geometric Duality of φ-Deformed Exponential Families
status_evidence.snippet: Geometric structures depend on the choice of deformation function φ.
status_evidence.claim: Deformation function/parameter is fixed prior to constructing the geometry.
